cases.description: Schema has no id (getId() returns null) and the ref does not start with "#/" nor "/". None of the conditional branches are taken, so the method should return the root schema node unchanged.

Schema has id "http://example.com/schemas/main". The ref starts with this id, so the first if strips the id leaving "#/defs/thing". The second if removes the leading "#", yielding "/defs/thing". The third if is true, the pointer is decoded (no change) and node.at("/defs/thing") returns an existing sub‑node. The method should return that sub‑node.

Schema id matches the beginning of the ref, stripping it leaves "/defs/thing" (no leading "#"). The second if is skipped, the third if processes the pointer, decodes it and node.at("/defs/thing") returns an existing sub‑node.

Schema has no id. The ref starts with "#/", so the second if removes the leading "#" producing "/components/schemas/Person". The third if then resolves the pointer and returns the corresponding sub‑node.
Schema has no id and the ref starts directly with "/". After decoding, node.at("/missing/path") yields a MissingNode, causing the method to call handleNullNode(ref, schema) and return its result.
Ref is exactly the schema id. After the first if the jsonPointer becomes an empty string. Neither the "#/" nor the "/" checks succeed, so the original schema node is returned.
Ref starts with "#" but not with "#/". The second if is false, the third if is also false, therefore the method returns the original schema node.
Ref is exactly "#/". After the second if the pointer becomes "/"; the third if processes it, node.at("/") returns the root node, which is the original schema node.

Ref starts with a leading "/" (no "#"). The method decodes (no change) and resolves the JSON Pointer to an existing sub‑node. The original schema has an id, but it does not match the ref, so the id‑stripping branch is skipped.
Ref contains an URL‑encoded slash. After the second if the pointer is "/defs%2Fthing"; the third if decodes it to "/defs/thing" and node.at resolves to the expected sub‑node.
Ref starts with "/" and includes an encoded slash. The pointer is decoded to "/defs/thing" and the method returns the corresponding node.
Empty string ref does not trigger any conditional branch; the method returns the root schema node unchanged.
Ref is a solitary "#" (no following "/"). Neither the second nor the third if conditions are satisfied, so the original schema node is returned.
Passing a null reference causes a NullPointerException when the method evaluates ref.startsWith(...).

Schema id is "http://example.com/schemas/main". The ref starts with this id, so the id is stripped leaving "Extra#/defs/thing". Because the remaining pointer does not start with "#" or "/", no further processing occurs and the original schema node is returned.
Ref starts with "#/"; after stripping it becomes "/missing/node". node.at("/missing/node") yields a MissingNode, causing the method to invoke handleNullNode(ref, schema) and return its result.
findSchemaResourceRoot() returns null, causing a NullPointerException when the method attempts to call schema.getId() or schema.getSchemaNode().
findSchemaResourceRoot() returns a non‑null JsonSchema, but its getSchemaNode() returns null. When the method reaches node.at(jsonPointer) it throws a NullPointerException because node is null.

The jsonPointer starts with '/' so the third if block is entered. The pointer contains an unescaped '~' character, which makes JsonNode.at() compile the pointer and throw an IllegalArgumentException. The method does not catch this exception, so it propagates.
